cues.en: Only a few elements can be permanent magnets. Iron is one. Copper is not. But if you pass an electric current through any metal, it becomes a magnet. An electromagnet. But how does this work? Well, strangely enough, it's a consequence of special relativity. Special relativity is the fact that in our universe, length and time aren't absolute. They're perceived differently by observers moving relative to each other, hence relativity.
cues.zh: 只有少数几种元素能成为永磁体。铁是其中之一，铜则不是。但如果让电流通过任何金属，它就会变成磁铁，也就是电磁铁。但这是怎么运作的呢？说来奇怪，这其实是狭义相对论的结果。狭义相对论指出，在我们的宇宙中，长度和时间并不是绝对的。相对运动的观察者所感知到的时空是不同的，这就是“相对”的含义。

cues.en: For example, if you measure carefully enough, you'll find that time passes slower for observers moving relative to you. And moving objects are also contracted in their direction of motion.
cues.zh: 例如，如果测量足够精确，你会发现相对于你运动的观察者，其时间流逝得更慢。同时，运动的物体也会在其运动方向上发生收缩。

cues.en: So when an object is moving relative to you, it actually takes up less space than when it's not moving. And even though this effect is obviously way tinier than we've shown, length contraction is what makes an electromagnet work. Picture a copper wire. It consists of positive metal ions swimming in a sea of free negative electrons. Now the number of protons is equal to the number of negative electrons, so overall the wire is neutral. So if there were a positive charge...
cues.zh: 因此，当一个物体相对于你运动时，它所占据的空间其实比它静止时要小。尽管这种效应显然比我们展示的要微弱得多，但尺缩效应正是电磁铁发挥作用的原因。想象一根铜导线，它由浸泡在自由负电子海洋中的金属正离子组成。质子的数量等于负电子的数量，所以导线整体呈电中性。因此，如果附近有一个带正电的……

cues.en: positively charged cat nearby, it would experience no force from the wire at all. And even if there were a current in the wire, the electrons would just be drifting in one direction, but the density of positive and negative charges would still be the same, and so the wire would be neutral, so no force on the kitty. But what if the cat starts moving? Imagine for simplicity that the cat is moving in the same direction as the electrons with the same velocity.
cues.zh: 一只带正电的猫咪在旁边，它完全不会受到导线施加的力。即使导线中有电流通过，电子也只是朝一个方向漂移，正负电荷的密度仍然相同，所以导线依然呈电中性，猫咪也就不会受力。但如果猫咪开始运动呢？为了简化起见，假设猫咪正以与电子相同的速度、朝相同的方向运动。

cues.en: Well now, in my frame of reference, the wire is still neutral and so there should be no force on the cat. But consider the same situation in her frame of reference. In the cat's frame of reference, the positive charges in the wire are moving, so according to special relativity, their separation will be ever so slightly contracted. Also, from this perspective, the electrons aren't moving, so they'll be more spread out than before. Remember, objects take up more space when they're not moving than when they are. These two changes together mean there's a higher density of positive charges in the wire.
cues.zh: 现在，在我的参考系中，导线仍然是电中性的，所以猫咪应该不受力。但在猫咪的参考系中来看同样的情况呢？在猫的参考系中，导线里的正电荷在运动，因此根据狭义相对论，它们之间的间距会发生极其微小的收缩。此外，从这个视角来看，电子是静止的，所以它们会比之前分散得更开。记住，物体静止时比运动时占据的空间更大。这两个变化叠加在一起，意味着导线中的正电荷密度变高了。

cues.en: so it's no longer neutral. It's positively charged, which means that the positively charged cat will feel a repulsive electric force from the wire. But in my frame of reference, this seems mysterious. There's no force on a stationary charged cat, but a moving cat is somehow repelled from this neutral wire. How do you account for that force?
cues.zh: 因此它不再是电中性的，而是带正电，这意味着带正电的猫咪会受到来自导线的静电排斥力。但在我的参考系看来，这显得不可思议。静止的带电猫不受力，但运动的猫却莫名其妙地被这根中性导线排斥了。你该如何解释这种力呢？

cues.en: Well, we say it is the magnetic force. And that's mainly because a wire with current in it deflects nearby magnets. So really, what this experiment shows is that a magnetic field is just an electric field viewed from a different frame of reference. In the cat's frame of reference, it is repelled from the wire due to the electric field created by the excess positive charges produced by the effects of length contraction. In my frame of reference, the cat is repelled from a neutral wire due to the magnetic field created by the current flowing in the wire.
cues.zh: 我们说是磁力。主要是因为载流导线会偏转附近的磁体。所以这个实验真正表明的是，磁场只是从不同参考系看到的电场。在猫的参考系中，它被导线排斥，因为长度收缩效应产生多余正电荷，从而形成电场。在我的参考系中，猫被一根中性导线排斥，因为导线中流动的电流产生了磁场。

cues.en: So whether you see it as an electric or a magnetic field just depends on your frame of reference, but in either case, the results are the same. So an electromagnet is an everyday example of special relativity in action.
cues.zh: 所以，你把它看成电场还是磁场，只取决于你的参考系；但无论哪种情况，结果都一样。所以电磁铁就是狭义相对论在日常生活中发挥作用的一个例子。

cues.en: Now that might seem crazy since electrons drift through wires at about 0.00000000001% the speed of light. So how can special relativity have anything to do with it? Well, the truth is there are enough electrons in a wire and the electric interaction is so amazingly strong that even the minuscule effects of length contraction can produce significant charge imbalances that produce a noticeable force. So special relativity explains electromag.
cues.zh: 这听起来可能很疯狂，因为电子在导线中的漂移速度大约只有光速的 0.00000000001%。那狭义相对论怎么会和它有关呢？事实是，导线中有足够多的电子，而且电相互作用强得惊人，以至于连长度收缩的微小效应都能产生显著的电荷不平衡，从而产生可察觉的力。所以，狭义相对论解释了电磁学。

cues.en: But what about permanent magnets? Yeah, I mean there can't be electrical currents flowing around inside lumps of rock, can there? Click here to go to MinutePhysics where we'll explore magnetite, compasses, and all the wizardry of permanent magnets.
cues.zh: 但永磁体呢？是啊，我的意思是，一块块岩石内部不可能有电流在流动，对吧？点击这里前往 MinutePhysics，我们会探索磁铁矿、指南针，以及永磁体的种种神奇之处。
